topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139419/workflows/feb351e1-7e49-410d-a1ee-27a572f0e50e/jobs/5877424

Job `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`, merge-queue run for ethereum-optimism/optimism#23771 (contracts-only change), 2026-11-10.

```
Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:392
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go:1196
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial/interop_fault_proofs_test.go:81
Error:       Received unexpected error:
             operation failed permanently after 5 attempts: not found
Messages:    invalid exec msg receipt not found
```

About 10s before the assertion, chain 902 reorged out the unsafe block (13) that carried the invalid exec message tx:

```
WARN L2 reorg: existing unsafe block does not match derived attributes from L1 component=supernode chain_id=902
  err="transaction 0 does not match ..." unsafe=ce53f5..f22801:13 pending_safe=ac50d9..a4c010:12
```

The mismatch is in the L1 info deposit (different L1 origin), so the tx is dropped and its receipt is never found. Looks like a race between sequencing and L1 derivation rather than a code regression. CircleCI insights also shows a failure in `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (1/100 runs on develop).

topIssues.title: kona-node: recover when the EL rejects a delegated forkchoice update
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

## Summary

When the execution layer (EL) rejects a delegated forkchoice update with `INVALID_FORKCHOICE_STATE`, kona-node needs a recovery policy. Both op-geth (`SetCanonical` before its finalized checks) and op-reth (`on_canonical_chain_update` before `ensure_consistent_forkchoice_state`) make the requested head canonical before rejecting it. A delegate whose head does not descend from kona-node's finalized block can therefore leave the EL on its fork after a rejected update, and kona-node's reset then walks a chain that misses its own finalized block.

This scope was split out of #24004 (#23910) and #24005 (#23911). Three Fable 5.1 xhigh review rounds showed that each recovery mechanism added there brought new edge cases. Those PRs keep the pre-existing behavior for a rejected forkchoice update, which is to reset the engine.

## Scope

- Classify a rejected delegated forkchoice update. Look up the engine's finalized block by hash to tell "the delegate's chain does not descend from finality" apart from "the EL lost finality". When the EL still holds finality, restore the EL's canonical chain by resending the engine's own forkchoice.
- Do not retry a rejected delegated head on every poll. Do not remember a transient rejection, such as a safe hash the EL has not stored yet.
- Blame the label that actually moved: a cross-safe-only update must not mark the local-safe head as rejected.
- Make the sync-start walk refuse a chain that is not on the finalized block (op-node `ReorgFinalizedErr` parity) without letting a delegate's head stop the node. Restore and retry. Classify only a genuine finality mismatch as retryable, and treat a missing L1 origin that is actually a fork as a fork.
- Add a `synchronize` backstop that keeps safe and local-safe at or above finalized, without making the reset path fatal.
- Correct a stale safe label even when the verified cross-safe head sits below it.

## Open findings carried over (from the round-3 Fable reviews of #24004 and #24005)

- `FinalityNotRestored` wraps permanent sync-start errors, so they are retried forever.
- A restoring forkchoice update rejected because the EL lost finality loops the reset.
- During EL sync, a different block in the EL at the delegated height does not prove divergence.
- A missing L1 origin at or below the finalized block is classed as temporary before the mismatch check runs.
- A transient `INVALID_FORKCHOICE_STATE` caused by a not-yet-stored safe hash is remembered until the next reset.
- `consolidate()` sends delegated updates through plain `synchronize`, so they are not classified.
- Blame is decided by whether an unsafe head was carried, not by which label was unproven.
- Safe-label rejections are not remembered, which costs three EL round-trips per poll.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A delegate's head cannot stop the node or loop the engine reset.
- [ ] Mocked Engine API tests in kona-engine for each case above, including an EL that has already made the rejected head canonical.
- [ ] Fable 5.1 xhigh review with no outstanding correctness findings.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run a subset of the super fault-proof tests on PR CI
topIssues.author: nonsense
topIssues.body:
The op-e2e super fault-proof tests (`op-e2e/faultproofs/super_test.go`) are the only tests that build the op-e2e interop SuperSystem and run its interop migration on the live L1. They need cannon, so PR CI skips them: they run only in the `develop-fault-proofs` workflow after merge, or on a branch through a `fault_proofs_dispatch` pipeline. A change that breaks the SuperSystem world or the migration is found only after it lands.

Port a few of these cases to sysgo, so they run on PR CI:

- create a super game
- play one full super game
- one step with a large preimage (the op-e2e version, `TestSuperCannonStepWithLargePreimage`, has been skipped since April 2025)

The `memory-all-*` acceptance jobs already build the cannon prestate and the kona binaries, and `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs` already plays super games on worlds that the same EIP-7702 helper (`op-e2e/e2eutils/transactions/setcode.go`) migrates. The other super fault-proof tests can stay post-merge.

Raised in the review of #23668, which moved the SuperSystem world from `interopgen` to op-deployer.

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: add eth-liquidity-pause command
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23348 (`karl/eth-liquidity-pause`). That PR makes `ETHLiquidity` mirror the chain's L1 pause through the permissionless `L1CrossDomainMessenger.syncETHLiquidityPause()`.

## What it's for

`op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause` is a small CLI for the ETHLiquidity pause. It has three uses:

- **Devnet gate `interop.eth-liquidity-pause`:** `devnet-pause` → `status --expect paused` → `devnet-unpause` → `status --expect unpaused`.
- **Production verification:** `status` is read-only and works on any chain. Production pausing stays with the guardian's existing DeputyPauseModule flow, and this tool never pauses production. Nothing new is needed in superchain-ops.
- **Mirroring an L1 pause (or unpause, or expiry) to L2:** `sync` is permissionless, so any funded key can run it.

## Commands

- **`status --l2 <rpc>... [--l1 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr>...] [--expect paused|unpaused] [--json]`**
  - For each chain it reads `ETHLiquidity.paused()` and `pausedL1Timestamp()`.
  - It runs an `eth_call` of `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH` with 1 wei. A state override funds the dummy `--from`, so the sender needs no balance. It reports whether the call reverts and with which error (selector and name).
  - With `--l1`, it also shows `L1CrossDomainMessenger.paused()`, which is the ETHLockbox pause, and prints `OUT OF SYNC` when L1 and L2 differ.
  - `--expect` exits non-zero on any mismatch. For `paused`, every chain needs `paused()` true, `sendETH` reverting with `ETHLiquidity_Paused()` and, if read, L1 paused.
- **`sync --l1 <rpc> --l2 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr> ... --key <any funded key>`**
  - Checks that each messenger's `SystemConfig.l2ChainId()` matches the `--l2` it is paired with.
  - Prints the L1 and L2 state per chain and skips chains already in sync (`--force` overrides).
  - Calls `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, waits for the L1 receipt, then polls L2 until `paused()` equals the L1 pause at the sync's block, or `--timeout` passes.
- **`devnet-pause` / `devnet-unpause --guardian-key <key>`**
  - Resolves each chain's ETHLockbox identifier through messenger → SystemConfig → portal → lockbox. Chains that share a lockbox are handled once.
  - Checks that the key is the SuperchainConfig guardian.
  - Calls `pause`, `extend` (if an earlier pause expired) or `unpause` on the lockbox identifier, then runs `sync`.
  - `devnet-unpause` warns if a global pause is still active.
  - Refuses OP Mainnet, Ink, Unichain, their Sepolia chains (10, 57073, 130, 11155420, 763373, 1301) and an L1 of Ethereum mainnet. There is no override flag.

Every flag can also come from `--config <toml>` (see `config.example.toml`). Local `*.toml` files in that directory are gitignored because they may hold keys.

## Usage

```bash
# Production / any chain: read-only
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status \
  --l2 https://mainnet.optimism.io --l2 <ink-rpc> --l2 <unichain-rpc> \
  --l1 <eth-rpc> --l1-messenger <op-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <ink-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <uni-l1cdm>

# Mirror the current L1 pause to L2 (permissionless)
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause sync --config pause.toml --key <funded-l1-key>

# Devnet gate
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-pause   --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect paused
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-unpause --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect unpaused
```

## Tests

None of these tests need a network.

- **Calldata:** encoding for `paused()`, `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, `sendETH`, and SuperchainConfig `pause`/`unpause`/`extend`/`pausable`/`paused(address)`.
- **ABI drift:** a test checks every hand-written signature and custom error against the contracts-bedrock ABI snapshots on this stack, so a rename in #23348 fails here.
- **Revert decoding:** custom errors and `Error(string)` reasons.
- **Safety checks:** production refusal, `--l2`/`--l1-messenger` pairing, grouping chains by shared lockbox, the guardian pause/extend/unpause choice, and `--expect` evaluation, including L1 paused while L2 is not synced.
- **Config loading:** TOML values load into each command, including the example config.
- **`status` end to end:** runs against in-process fake L1/L2 JSON-RPC servers. The cases are paused and synced, unpaused, out of sync, a pre-pause ETHLiquidity, a messenger paired with the wrong chain, and JSON output. The fake rejects `sendETH` without the balance override, as geth does.
- **`sync` end to end:** runs on geth simulated backends with mock contracts. The cases are skip when in sync, `--force` send and wait for L2, a reverting call never sent, and an L2 timeout.

```
go test ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # ok
go vet ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...    # clean
./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # 0 issues
go mod tidy -diff                                    # clean
```

I also ran `status` read-only against OP Mainnet and OP Sepolia public RPCs. ETHLiquidity is not initialized there yet, and the tool reports `Error("Proxy: implementation not initialized")` for both reads.

**Not run:** `sync` and `devnet-*` against a live devnet with #23348 deployed. The guardian path (`devnet-pause`/`devnet-unpause`) has unit coverage only for its decision logic.

topPRs.title: op-reth: warm the proofs-history page cache ahead of persistence
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #24055; this PR contains its commit too. Review only the commits after it.

The proofs-history engine persists on a single thread. It reads B-tree pages one at a time through mmap faults, so on network-attached disks it waits on one read of about 1 ms at a time. On op-mainnet hardware (n4-standard-16, Hyperdisk Balanced 20k IOPS) persisting a block waits on about 900 to 1,200 such reads and takes about 700 ms, while the disk runs far below its IOPS limit and the CPUs are idle. During heavy periods the engine cannot keep up and proofs fall behind the tip. This PR reads the same pages earlier, from parallel read-only transactions, so the persistence transaction finds them in the page cache.

Effect on operators: none by default. `--proofs-history.prefetch-threads N` (default 0, off; 0–64) enables warming:
- When a block enters the engine's buffer, the pages its write will touch are read.
- When a batch has been persisted, the pages the prunes of the next two batches will touch are read. Two batches, so that a prune's pages are read a whole batch before it runs.
- Warming only reads. Work that is dropped, late or failed costs performance, never correctness.

Measured on a pair of op-mainnet followers with production hardware (devnets-private#2562), with 8 threads. Each row compares the two nodes over the same blocks.

At the tip, persistence time per block:

| | control | with warming |
|---|---|---|
| first commit | 721 ms | 244 ms |
| second commit | 645 ms | 190 ms |
| second commit, ten minutes of heavier blocks (about twice the keys) | 1,354 ms | 323 ms |

In the second commit's 190 ms the write takes 25 ms, the prune 89 ms and the commit 76 ms; the control spends 110, 459 and 76 ms. The persistence thread waits on about 70 disk reads per block instead of about 790.

One node catching up, so that persistence was saturated, persisted 1.44 blocks per second before, 2.6 to 2.8 with the first commit and 2.7 with the second. The first commit left about 260 reads per block in the prune, because its prune pass started when the previous batch finished and scanned changesets on one thread. The second commit removed them (prune 280 to 80 ms per block), and the limit moved to the disk: at 2.7 blocks per second it runs at its provisioned 20,000 IOPS, with about 4,800 page writes and 1,300 reads per block, so commits wait on their writes (71 to 199 ms per block). Catching up also re-executes each block on the engine thread, which takes about 310 ms per block.

New metrics:
- `reth_optimism_trie_engine_prefetch_{write,prune}_duration_seconds` and `..._{write,prune}_keys_total`.
- `reth_optimism_trie_engine_prefetch_dropped_jobs_total`: block writes that were not warmed because warming fell behind persistence. `..._failed_jobs_total`: warming jobs that failed.
- `reth_optimism_trie_storage_phase_major_faults{operation,phase,table}` and `reth_optimism_trie_storage_write_state_major_faults`: major page faults on the persistence thread per phase, which are the disk reads it waited on. They are read from `/proc/thread-self/stat` and are `0` off Linux.

Choices the diff does not explain:
- The store receives the block diff and a block range, not key lists, so it derives the keys the way its own write and prune paths do. Tests compare the warmed keys with the keys those paths record.
- When warming falls behind, the queue drops the oldest buffered block and serves prune passes first. The oldest block is persisted soonest, so warming it helps least, and the prune is the larger share of persistence time.
- Each job spawns scoped threads instead of using a pool. A spawn costs microseconds against reads of about a millisecond, and the crate gets no new dependency.
- The live test marks each block as persisted by reth (the `Finish` checkpoint), because the pruner never prunes past reth's persisted head. Without that, no prune ran in the live tests.

Reviews: `rust-code-reviewer` ran on both commits. The second commit fixes its findings on the first: the queue policy under overload, the prune range arithmetic, a warming thread that a panic could end, the API shape, and missing tests. On the second commit it found no high-severity issue. Fixed from that review: blocks that stayed queued after an unwind or after a save completed outside the event loop (the queue now holds the buffer's blocks weakly), tests for the pass limit, a moved window and the completed-save hook, and smaller simplifications.

Dismissed, with the author's confirmation:
- A failure to spawn the warming thread panics at startup. The engine's two other service threads do the same, and one of them is spawned next.
- A save that completes while the engine waits for it (unwind, shutdown) does not request a prune pass. Each pass covers two batches, so the next completed save makes up for it.
- Blocks in the batch being saved are still warmed. A batch is written in order, so its later blocks still benefit.
- `spawn_with_thresholds` could be folded into `spawn_with_config`. It predates this PR, and the exex tests use it.
- The live test does not assert that warming ran. Unit tests assert each hook (`buffered_blocks_are_warmed`, `completed_saves_warm_the_next_prunes`, the prefetcher tests); the live test checks that persistence and pruning stay correct with warming on.

topPRs.title: kona-engine,kona-node-service: recover when the EL rejects a delegated forkchoice update
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
A delegate whose chain does not descend from kona-node's finalized block can leave the EL on its fork after a rejected forkchoice update, because op-geth and op-reth make the head canonical before rejecting it; the next reset then walks a chain that misses finality.

On every delegated path, a rejected update that moved the head restores the engine's own forkchoice while the EL holds the finalized block by hash, and is permanent; a restore answered `SYNCING` or rejected resets instead. After a rejection on a chain that forks below finality, the delegate actor holds the delegate's heads back as a whole until the engine's finality moves, otherwise every five minutes, or until a reset. A rejection that moved only the safe label restores nothing and is retried next poll. The sync start refuses a chain off the finalized block (op-node `ReorgFinalizedErr`), also when the sequencing window stops the walk above it; a reset restores the engine's finalized block, or after a restart the EL's own, so a delegate's head cannot stop the node. A missing block or L1 origin at the finalized height is retried while the provider lags; an L1 origin on another chain stops the node. `synchronize` keeps the safe labels at or above finality.

BREAKING CHANGE: `ConsolidateTaskError` gains `DelegatedForkchoiceRejected { heads, rejection }` and `FailedToFetchFinalizedBlock`; `SynchronizeTaskError` gains `FinalizedAheadOfSafe`; `SyncStartError::MismatchedFinalizedBlock` becomes `{ finalized, walked }` and `SyncStartError` gains `FinalizedHeightUnavailable`, `FinalizedL1OriginUnavailable`, `FinalizedL1OriginNotServedByHash` and `FinalizedL1OriginNotCanonical`; `EngineResetError` gains `FinalityNotRestored`; `EngineDerivationClient` gains `send_rejected_delegated_safe_heads`; `DerivationActorRequest` gains `ProcessRejectedDelegatedSafeHeads`; `DelegatedRejection` and `SafeLabel` are exported.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/24061. Stacked on #24007.

topPRs.title: rust!: Update reth to v2.7.0
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
Closes #23404. This is the first of the version-by-version reth bumps; v2.8.x and v2.9.0 follow.

## What

Updates reth to v2.7.0 through the `op-v2.7.0` fork branch. The pin is a `rev` on the fork stack ethereum-optimism/reth#34 → ethereum-optimism/reth#35 → ethereum-optimism/reth#40 → ethereum-optimism/reth#41 (`0447ceb`) until that stack merges and `op-v2.7.0-0` is tagged. Two of them carry `op-v2.6.0` patches that v2.7.0 lacks: ethereum-optimism/reth#40 the trie seek boundary fix (`paradigmxyz/reth#28264`), and ethereum-optimism/reth#41 the RPC replay through the block executor (ethereum-optimism/reth#37, a backport of `paradigmxyz/reth#28266`) that #23942's `rpc_replay_settlement` tests depend on.

Changes beyond the version sync:

- API adaptations:
  - `StateProviderDatabase` takes an `EvmStateProvider` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27109`).
  - `CancelOnDrop` moved to `reth-tasks` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27466`).
  - `StateProviderFactory` has a `Primitives` type (`paradigmxyz/reth#26923`).
  - `BlockAndReceipts` holds `SharedReceipts` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27427`).
  - The e2e setup functions folded into `E2ETestSetupBuilder` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27432`).
- `reth-optimism-rpc` vendors reth v2.6.0's `MemoryOverlayStateProvider` for the flashblocks pending state (see How).
- op-reth denies the new `--rpc-cache.max-bals-bytes`, like every other block access list option.
- Two mirrored upstream symbols changed: the proofs buffer's copy of the deleted `MemoryOverlayStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state` becomes a frozen `port`, and the proofs-history `get_proof` copy notes why it doesn't follow upstream's new `spawn_blocking_io_with_state`.
- `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` gains what building the `op-v2.7.0` fork branch needed.

## Why

Keeps op-reth on a supported reth line.

## How

`paradigmxyz/reth#26923` removed `MemoryOverlayStateProvider`, and its replacement, `state_with_block_appended`, can't open the pending state of a speculative flashblock build. With canonical head N-1, a build can run several blocks ahead: N+1 on pending N, and so on. The tip's header names pending N as its parent, which reth's overlay doesn't know, while its bundle holds every write since the anchor N-1. Passing N fails with `BlockHashNotFound`, and passing N-1 panics on the parent `debug_assert` in `OverlayBuilder::with_appended_block`. The vendored provider layers the tip on `history_by_block_hash(anchor)` as before. The commits show it in order: the compiling API change, a red test of the speculative case, then the fix. `op-reth-test-engine` uses `state_with_block_appended` directly, since its blocks link to real parents in the overlay manager it shares with its provider.

**Review request:** the agentic sweep from `docs/ai/reth-update-review.md` (`reth-update-reviewer`, full-range and forward) has not run on this PR. Please run it. Two leads:

1. `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` is now on by default (`paradigmxyz/reth#27447`), sharing recovered senders between transaction ingress and payload execution. Check that recovery through the cache matches the uncached path for deposits (0x7E) and post-exec transactions (0x7D).
2. Upstream's new `LoadState::spawn_blocking_io_with_state` builds pending state through `state_with_block_appended` for a `PendingStateSource::Block`. Check that every `pending` state query still reaches the vendored overlay through `OpEthApi::local_pending_state`.

## Caveats

- Operator-facing CLI changes inherited from reth v2.7.0. No flags are removed:
  - New: `--rpc-cache.max-blocks-bytes` (2 GiB), `--rpc-cache.max-receipts-bytes` (1 GiB), `--rpc-cache.idle-timeout` (1h), and `--engine.backfill-threshold` (32, as before).
  - Lower defaults: `--rpc-cache.max-blocks` 5000 → 1000, `--rpc-cache.max-receipts` 2000 → 500.
  - `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` is on by default. `--engine.sender-recovery-cache=false` turns it off.
  - `--rpc.gascap` (default 50M) now also caps `eth_estimateGas`.
  - `--rpc.max-tracing-requests`, `--rpc.max-blocking-io-requests` and `--rpc.proof-permits` reject `0`.
- RPC: a state query for a block whose changesets are pruned now fails with code `4444` and "pruned history unavailable: requested N, earliest available M" (`paradigmxyz/reth#27367`). It used to be an internal error (`-32603`, "insufficient changesets..."). Nothing in this repo matches either. External clients matching the old text need updating.
- `alloy-trie` stays at 0.9.7 in both lockfiles. The declared range (`0.9.4`, as in reth) admits 0.9.9, which breaks `reth-trie-common` at this reth version (`HashBuilder::all_branch_nodes`), so don't refresh it with a broad `cargo update`.
- The bump changes code that both proof programs run (revm, alloy and kona's executor). The next kona-sp1 build has a new super-aggregation vkey, and the next kona client build has a new Cannon prestate. Releasing either needs the matching `absolutePrestate` in the dispute game args updated on-chain, before or as proposers switch: a proposer whose proofs don't verify against the configured prestate loses its challenged games.
- `eth/memory_overlay.rs` keeps upstream's three `TODO: Currently this does not reuse available in-memory trie nodes.` comments. We don't plan to resolve them:
  - The file is a copy of upstream, kept close so it can be compared with upstream.
  - The gap doesn't apply to its only use: flashblock `ExecutedBlock`s carry no trie updates, so there are no in-memory nodes to reuse.
  - The copy goes away with #23998, or once reth's API can append a chain of blocks.

## Alternatives

- For the flashblocks pending state, several ways to stay on reth's new overlay were considered and dropped:
  - Rewriting the tip's header parent to the anchor breaks the overlay's assumption that parent numbers are consecutive (`parent_num_hash`).
  - Feeding speculative blocks into the engine's overlay manager would mix unvalidated, cumulative-diff blocks into engine state.
  - Folding the whole speculative chain through `OverlayBuilder::with_appended_block` needs both the chain at the RPC (#23998) and reth access we don't have: `state_with_block_appended` takes one block, and `ProviderFactory::overlay_manager` is crate-private.

## Potential follow-ups

- #23998: transactions in earlier speculative flashblock blocks disappear from RPC lookups, and the RPC's pending value isn't reset when speculative state is cleared.
